subject: Post-demo: Time-to-first-token targets & streaming cadence (Atlas Labs)
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@atlaslabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Time-to-first-token targets & streaming cadence (Atlas Labs)

Hi Priya — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the asks we heard so we have a clean handoff to engineering: 

- Primary perf goal: Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for short prompts (1–20 tokens) <= 250 ms P50, <= 450 ms P95 under steady-state.
- Burst/scale: baseline concurrency 60 req/s for web clients, ability to sustain short bursts to 180 req/s for <2 minutes.
- Streaming: web clients prefer SSE; mobile app will likely use WebSocket as a fallback. We should support both and auto-fallback if SSE handshake fails.
- Chunk cadence: target chunk emission every 200–300 ms for typical responses, with a maximum chunk size of ~256 tokens to avoid large blocking latencies.
- Acceptance telemetry: per-token latency, P50/P95/P99 of first byte and first token, tracing id in headers, and token counts in response.

I've attached Atlas' sample prompt set and our initial TTFT probe plan. Next steps we proposed on the call:
1) Tech spike to validate SSE handshake and chunk cadence under representative load (owner: Karthik).
2) Pilot environment: dedicated pilot capacity for 48 hours with your sample prompts and synthetic concurrency to validate SLOs.
3) Telemetry contract: agree on the minimal telemetry fields and sample rates (we suggested 1% full trace + 10% condensed).

Can you confirm these priorities and give us the name/email of the engineer who will join the spike? Also let us know if the TTFT targets above are firm or negotiable — we can tune tradeoffs (quantization, batching) once we know the strict target.

Thanks — Michael
Michael Grant
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.com

From: Priya Sharma <priya@atlaslabs.com>

Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Time-to-first-token targets & streaming cadence (Atlas Labs)

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming priorities and adding a couple clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT target: we need <= 250 ms P50 for short prompts and <= 500 ms P95 for production traffic. P99 is less critical for now but should be tracked.
- Concurrency: baseline 60 req/s (global), but our peak traffic windows can spike to 180 req/s for ~90–120s. We want graceful degradation (e.g., degrade chunk cadence before dropping requests).
- Streaming modes: web clients should use SSE. Mobile SDK will default to WebSocket; fallback to non-streaming if connection is flaky.
- Chunk cadence goal: 200 ms ideal, acceptable range 150–350 ms depending on network and model load. We care more about consistent cadence than absolute minimum latency for later tokens.

We're happy to provide an internal engineer for the spike — please loop in Sahil (sahil@atlaslabs.com). For the pilot, we can spin up a staging API key and share a short-lived test token.

A couple asks from our infra/security team:
- We need a list of what telemetry is captured and whether PII appears in traces (we'll redact as needed).
- Does Redwood support IP allowlisting for the pilot endpoints?

I'll confirm Sahil's availability for a spike on Tuesday/Wednesday next week.

Best,
Priya
Head of Product, Atlas Labs
priya@atlaslabs.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@atlaslabs.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Time-to-first-token targets & streaming cadence (Atlas Labs)

Thanks — good notes. Technical thoughts / feasibility and proposed test plan: 

1) Feasibility: the targets (<=250ms P50, <=500ms P95) are achievable with a few levers: warm resident workers, KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, and modest quantization (int8) on the model we propose. Batching helps throughput but increases TTFT; we'll avoid batch delays for the first token by prioritizing fast path execution for single-request emits.

2) Streaming implementation: Redwood supports SSE and WebSocket simultaneously. We'll prefer SSE for browser clients (smaller handshake) and route mobile-origin traffic to WS. We already have auto-fallback policies that detect handshake failure and fall back to polling/non-streaming if streaming can't be established.

3) Chunk cadence: we can target 200–250 ms cadence on average by tuning the emitter cadence and limiting chunk token size to ~64 tokens typical (~256 hard max). We'll instrument per-emit timestamps to measure cadence drift.

4) Concurrency and burst: for pilot, propose a 4x-GPU dedicated pool (NVIDIA A10G or equivalent) with autoscale headroom. With the above config we can hit 60 steady req/s with 180 short bursts for the 2-minute window. We'll validate with load tests.

5) Acceptance criteria (suggested): run 48-hour pilot, run templated workload from atlas-sample-prompt-set.csv with realistic jitter: if TTFT P50 <= 250ms and P95 <= 500ms for >95% of test windows and chunk cadence median within 200–300ms, consider acceptance. We will surface per-request traces and aggregate histograms.

6) Security/ops: we support IP allowlisting for pilot endpoints and can redact PII in traces if you mark sample prompts. We'll send a short telemetry schema doc prior to the spike.

Action items: 
- Karthik to own the tech spike (this week).
- Priya to provide Sahil's contact and confirm staging token.
- Michael to schedule the spike kickoff and provide the probe harness link.

I'll prepare a short test harness (link below) and a runbook for the pilot.
